correctness.rationale: Every source vector has squared norm 3 and total coordinate sum 1. For equal source edges distinct points have inner product -1. For distinct simple-graph edges disjoint supports yield inner product 0, while a unique shared endpoint yields the product of signs ±1; hence all different-vertex squared distances are 4,6,8 and maximum 8 is realized. Counting within-edge triangles and four opposite-sign pairs per incident edge pair proves the diameter-edge formula. A four-clique would have Gram diagonal 3 and off-diagonal -1 so its vector sum has squared norm zero, contradicting total coordinate sum four; triangles exist. At any graph node v, the negative-sign vertex on any incident edge is forced to the third colour of the two positive-sign vertices on another incident edge. This makes its colour independent of the edge and defines a proper G-colouring. Conversely each proper G-colouring uniquely assigns the negative-sign point colours and the third triangle colour, satisfying every cross-incidence diameter edge. Therefore the maps invert exactly. Exact pure-Python finite checks passed 2,627,773 assertions across all 771 connected labelled simple graphs on 2–5 vertices, and independently compared counts on 2–4 vertices. Finite testing does not stand in place of the unrestricted proof. Complexity follows from the standard connected graph 3-COL reduction. No nonstandard infinite external lemma is needed.

originality.rationale: Direct comparison with the motivating manuscript arXiv:2605.23371v1 (Section 2.2, Section 3 and Section 4), the complete accessible text of arXiv:2209.08069v2 (face criteria and edge counts), arXiv:2603.03894v1 (dual and canonical form), and the full public published-finding corpus circumradius record found no graph of *maximum Euclidean-distance pairs* or proper three-colouring bijection. The circumradius theorem proves all vertices lie on a common optimal sphere but explicitly leaves their pairwise distance spectrum uncomputed: common radius does not constrain adjacency by farthest-pair distance. Source-edge and ordinary one-skeleton counts do not imply graph colouring of this different distance graph. The actual published-finding corpus queries and local ledger deduplication found no covering record. Priority is provisional and an unindexed equivalent presentation remains a risk.

value.rationale: The Euclidean farthest-pair graph of a natural, recently studied graph-based lattice polytope is not its ordinary one-skeleton. A complete distance-graph reconstruction formula with the exact proper labelled 3-colouring bijection creates a structural bridge from metric geometry to vertex colouring. It proves K4-freeness alongside NP-completeness in an explicitly parameterized family, and preserves the exact number of 3-colourings. These are natural, nonlocal invariants of all source graphs and explain computational richness despite constant diameter and graph-independent enclosing radius, not merely a numerical example or routine normalisation.
